source.title: Paper page - MultiWorld: Scalable Multi-Agent Multi-View Video World Models
source.author: Haoyu Wu ,

athena.directive: The Creative Liberation Engine shall develop and integrate a self-hosted, scalable multi-agent, multi-view video world model, inspired by MultiWorld, to serve as its foundational simulation and training environment, ensuring complete control over its operational parameters and data generation capabilities.
athena.rationale: To achieve true autonomy and self-improvement, the Creative Liberation Engine requires a robust, self-owned simulation environment that can accurately model complex multi-agent interactions and diverse perspectives. This aligns with Article I (Sovereignty) by avoiding reliance on external, proprietary systems. By aiming for a complete implementation (Article IV), we ensure a high-quality, production-ready system from the outset, enabling automated agent training and testing, thus supporting Article XX (Zero human wait time).

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine's Sovereign World Model
options.description: Develop a core, self-hosted world model within the Creative Liberation Engine, directly implementing and advancing the principles of MultiWorld (scalable multi-agent, multi-view, action-controllable, multi-view-consistent video generation). This model will be the authoritative source for simulating complex environments and agent interactions for all Creative Liberation Engine operations, including training, validation, and hypothetical scenario generation.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant initial investment in research, development, and computational resources. However, it provides complete control, customization, and long-term strategic advantage by owning the foundational simulation layer.

options.title: Modular Simulation Core for Agent Experimentation
options.description: Construct a modular simulation framework capable of integrating various world model components, including those inspired by MultiWorld. This approach focuses on creating a flexible architecture where different world models, agent policies, and rendering techniques can be swapped and experimented with, ensuring the system can evolve with future research.
options.tradeoffs: Potentially slower to reach a fully integrated, high-fidelity world model compared to a direct implementation. Offers superior adaptability and extensibility for future research directions.

options.title: Advanced Agent Identity & Latent Space Coherence
options.description: Prioritize the development of a dedicated sub-system focused on robust agent identity encoding and maintaining action-controllable coherence within shared latent spaces, drawing heavily from MultiWorld's AIE (Agent Identity Embeddings) concepts. This component would ensure distinct yet interactive agent behaviors across multi-view scenarios, serving as a critical foundation for any multi-agent world model.
options.tradeoffs: Addresses only a specific, albeit crucial, aspect of a full world model. Requires seamless integration with other components responsible for video generation and physics.

options.title: Synthetic Data Generation for Creative Liberation Engine Perception
options.description: Implement a specialized module inspired by MultiWorld's video generation capabilities to produce highly realistic, action-controllable, multi-view synthetic video datasets. This data would be primarily used to train and validate Creative Liberation Engine's perception and vision systems, reducing reliance on costly real-world data collection.
options.tradeoffs: Focuses solely on data generation, not a full interactive simulation environment for agents. While invaluable for perception, it doesn't directly provide a dynamic interaction space for training agent policies.

options.title: External Engine Integration for Rapid Prototyping
options.description: Explore and integrate with existing high-fidelity game engines or simulation platforms (e.g., Unity, Unreal Engine) to rapidly prototype multi-agent, multi-view environments. MultiWorld's principles would guide the design of agent control and view consistency within these external platforms.
options.tradeoffs: Violates Article I (Sovereignty) by relying on third-party solutions. While faster for initial prototyping, it introduces dependencies and limits long-term control and deep customization.
